original_question: Which 3-regular graphs G occur as the underlying graph of a closed geodesic net on the round 3-sphere? Here a closed geodesic net is a geodesic net with no unbalanced vertices.
target_in_paper: Problem 2.0.2: classify all 3-regular graphs G such that the round 3-sphere has a geodesic net modelled on G.
correct_elements: The draft has identified the correct open problem from Section 2: it asks about 3-regular graphs, the round 3-sphere, and realization as a closed geodesic net. The parenthetical explanation of 'closed geodesic net' as having no unbalanced vertices matches the paper's terminology for nets with empty boundary set.
missing_details: The paper states this as a classification problem: classify all such graphs G, not just ask informally which ones occur.
Under the paper's standing conventions, the graph should be finite and connected.
The paper's formulation is 'the round 3-sphere has a geodesic net modelled on G', so the realization is as an embedded geodesic net with abstract model G.
A geodesic net here is embedded rather than immersed: edges are distinct non-constant geodesics, and edges are not allowed to intersect or self-intersect except at common endpoints.
Because the net is closed, every vertex is balanced; the balancing condition should be made explicit: at each vertex, the sum of the outgoing unit tangent vectors along all incident edges is zero.
This is about geodesic nets, not geodesic multinets, so no edge multiplicities or overlapping coincident edges are allowed.
The ambient metric should be specified as the standard round metric on S^3.
refined_question: Classify all finite connected 3-regular graphs G for which the standard round 3-sphere S^3 admits a connected embedded closed geodesic net modelled on G; that is, determine exactly which such G can be realized by an embedding into S^3 whose edges are distinct non-constant geodesic arcs, with no self-intersections or edge crossings except at common endpoints, and such that at every vertex the sum of the outgoing unit tangent vectors of the three incident edges is zero.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, classify all finite connected 3-regular graphs G for which there exists a smooth embedding of G into the round S^3 that is a critical point of the total-length functional under all smooth one-parameter diffeomorphic variations of S^3, with empty boundary set.
justification: This draft is clearly aiming at Section 2, Problem 2.0.2, because it asks for the combinatorial types of 3-regular graphs realized by closed geodesic nets on the round 3-sphere. The nearby opening of Section 2 supplies the meaning of 'closed geodesic net' as a net with empty boundary set. Section 1.1 then gives the exact definition of a geodesic net, the balancing condition, and the standing conventions used throughout the paper, including embeddedness and connectedness. I therefore kept the question narrowly on the paper's exact classification problem and only added the implicit definitional material needed to make it fully stand-alone, without broadening it to multinets, other manifolds, or higher-dimensional spheres.
